request: The app only has a home page and an about page, so there is nowhere to send visitors who want to get in touch. Add a new /contact route that renders inside the shared layout, with a heading and a short paragraph, and add a Contact link to the primary navigation so the page is reachable. Make sure the app still builds, the pages still render, and the tests pass.

plan.goal: Give the app a contact page the primary navigation can reach, so visitors have somewhere to find how to get in touch.

scope.title: A /contact route and its nav entry
scope.description: Add src/pages/Contact.tsx that renders an h1 heading, a short paragraph, and a link back to the home page, register it as a child route at path "contact" in src/App.tsx, and add a NavLink to /contact in src/layouts/Layout.tsx so the page is reachable from every view.

steps.description: Create src/pages/Contact.tsx with a heading, a short paragraph of how to get in touch, and a Link back to /.
Add a { path: 'contact', element: <Contact /> } entry to the children array in src/App.tsx so the component renders inside the shared layout.
Add a <NavLink to="/contact">Contact</NavLink> list item to the primary navigation in src/layouts/Layout.tsx.
Run the build and the test suite to confirm the app compiles, the home and about routes still render, and the existing tests pass.

out_of_scope.item: Adding a contact form that posts somewhere
out_of_scope.reason: A form needs an endpoint and validation; the request is for a page that explains how to get in touch, not a submission flow.

out_of_scope.item: Restructuring the router into nested or lazy routes
out_of_scope.reason: The starter registers routes as flat children of the layout; a router restructure is a larger change than adding one page.
